podcast.body: The song "Paranoid" itself was composed, recorded, and prepared in just 30 minutes, illustrating the band's continued commitment to spontaneity and directness as core elements of their value. "la paranoïla canción concretamente fue grabada compuesta y preparada en 30 minutos."

podcast.body: This song was included in the playlists used during the First Gulf War, which started in 1990, to subject Iraqi prisoners of war to prolonged periods of metal music. "ACDC shook me all night long, paranoid from Black Sabbath, and no more Mr. Nice Guy from Alice Cooper were some of the songs on those playlists."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This track stands as Black Sabbath's sole Top 20 hit. Its urgent and intense sound was noted as potentially unsettling, particularly to parents hearing it in late summer 1970. While not overtly "evil" in its lyrical content compared to other songs like "N.I.B.," its sonic intensity contributed to the band's overall scary appeal. "That is the only top 20 hit that black Sabbath ever had."
